title: Draft: OSI COTP: Dissect TLS over COTP
description:
Dissect TLS over COTP to the heuristic subdissector list. This
requires setting a conversation for COTP so that when the TLS dissector
calls find_or_create_conversation and conversation_set_dissector that
the TLS dissector is set to the COTP conversation, and not to the
underlying TCP conversation (which would prevent TPKT and COTP from
being properly called first.

That is a stopgap; thanks to db91d83def60efab743e5025e76e68cb6022ffbf
we should be able to use assign the dst-ref to the packet as a
port type instead of special handing in the packet_info.

Since the COTP dissector does not handle protocols that need to be
defragmented by the underlying transport, the sample file in #21350
breaks down at some point for some of the streams, where TLS records
are fragmented over COTP TSDUs (which is separate from the TSDUs being
fragmented into TPDUs, or from the TPDUs carried in TPKT being segmented
at the TCP layer. Also separate from the decrypted TLS application
payload being fragmented.) At that point it starts displaying TLS
Continuation Data.

Ping #21350 (which has a sample that includes a DSB for the first TLS
stream.)

commits_data.message:
OSI COTP: Dissect TLS over COTP

Dissect TLS over COTP to the heuristic subdissector list. This
requires setting a conversation for COTP so that when the TLS dissector
calls find_or_create_conversation and conversation_set_dissector that
the TLS dissector is set to the COTP conversation, and not to the
underlying TCP conversation (which would prevent TPKT and COTP from
being properly called first.

That is a stopgap; thanks to db91d83def60efab743e5025e76e68cb6022ffbf
we should be able to use assign the dst-ref to the packet as a
port type instead of special handing in the packet_info.

Since the COTP dissector does not handle protocols that need to be
defragmented by the underlying transport, the sample file in #21350
breaks down at some point for some of the streams, where TLS records
are fragmented over COTP TSDUs (which is separate from the TSDUs being
fragmented into TPDUs, or from the TPDUs carried in TPKT being segmented
at the TCP layer. Also separate from the decrypted TLS application
payload being fragmented.) At that point it starts displaying TLS
Continuation Data.

Ping #21350 (which has a sample that includes a DSB for the first TLS
stream.)
